findings.description: The DEVELOPMENT engine called entry_exit_return(t) while building the ranking eligibility rows. The future return value was carried with the row but ranking used only lagged FLOW and symbol tie-break. Exit-price availability therefore could have affected eligibility if an exit observation had been missing.
findings.evidence: The frozen DEVELOPMENT result reports exactly 12 eligible assets in every one of 102 periods and no data-integrity failure. Therefore no candidate was excluded by missing exit availability in the observed run.
findings.limitation: This is a provenance conclusion from the frozen run evidence, not a post-result rerun. V1 must not be rerun or altered to improve its outcome.

findings.description: The generic V1 engine accepted a TEMPORAL_HOLDOUT stage without independently requiring canonical DEVELOPMENT PASS evidence.
findings.evidence: The first DEVELOPMENT collector was hard-limited to 2023-01..2024-12. The runner required DEVELOPMENT, the exact development range, holdoutLoaded=false and postDevelopmentDataLoaded=false. The frozen result records both flags false.
findings.limitation: The engine-level guard was missing, so equivalent guards must be implemented prospectively before first PnL in any successor.
